pamphlet_excerpts: Prevention Way Avoid: Prevention is the best way to avoid cuts, nicks, andother injuries.
However Working Wood: However, as a Scout working with wood and knives, you should be prepared in the event of a cut or perhaps a splinter.
Stay Calm Adultin: If you are injured, stay calm and let the adultin charge know what has happened.
Accidents Happen: Sometimes accidents happen even when all safetyprecautions are taken.
step_by_step_procedure: Serious Cut Gash: For a serious cut or gash, seekmedical help immediately.
Minor Cuts Scrapes: For minor cuts and scrapes, follow these first aid steps: Step 1, Stop the bleeding by applying pressure with a clean, absorbent cloth; if cloth.
Blood Soaks Apply: Step 2, If the blood soaks through, apply a second bandage on top.
Not Off Bandage: Do not take off the first bandage becausethat will disturb the clotting that has already taken place.

pamphlet_excerpts: Don Own Tools: While you don’t need your own tools to earn this meritbadge, you should have a general knowledge of caringfor and sharpening the tools you use.
Knives Mustbe Sharpened: Most knives mustbe sharpened before use, and doing a good job couldtake a couple of hours.
Check Tools Dirt: Check tools for dirt and rust on a regular basis.
Apocketknife Carry Pocket: Apocketknife that you carry in your pocket may also pickup lint.
step_by_step_procedure: Light Coat Honing: Use a light coat of honing oil and let it set forawhile.
Tools Possible Condition: Keep tools in the best possible condition by makingsure they are dry.
Wipe Off Fingerprint: Wipe off fingerprint marks and moisture with a dry cloth.
Apply Couple Drops: Apply a couple of drops of oil tothe blades and joints of a knife.

pamphlet_excerpts: Carving Round Project: Carving in the Round First Project: Practice Stick This project is a practice stick that can help you learnhow to use a knife.
Piece Wood By-: Step 1, Get a piece of wood, 3⁄4-by-3⁄4-inch and 6 inches long.
Come Down Side: Step 2, Come down the side of the stick 3⁄4 inch, making a box on all four sides.
Repeat Times Creating: Repeat this three to four times, creating 3⁄4-inch squares down the stick.
step_by_step_procedure: Leaveyou Portion Stick: This will leaveyou a portion of the stick to hold onto.
Top Box Draw: Step 3, In the top box, draw the same design on all foursides of the stick.
Pick New Shape: Pick a new shape and repeat this inthe next square down, then all around the stick.
Repetition Youpractice Doing: This repetition will give youpractice doing similar cuts over and over again.

pamphlet_excerpts: Few Tools Areneeded: Very few tools areneeded to create beautiful designs, so almost anyone cancreate a work of art after learning the basics. with your owndesigns.
Sureto Firmly Securethe: Be sureto firmly securethe staff with avise clamp beforeyou start to work.
Intricate Designs Chip: The intricate designs of chip carving are created with a combination of simple shapes like triangles, diamonds, and squares.
Triangle Formed Cuts: A triangle is formed with three cuts madediagonally toward a central point, which creates an insideout pyramid.
step_by_step_procedure: Adding Cuts Point: Adding two cuts from a point outside one flatside creates a diamond.
Cut Side Squaremakes: One cut from each side of a squaremakes a square pyramid.
Pattern Drawn Straight: Any pattern that can be drawn with straight linescan be made into a chip carving design.
Several Different Knives: Several different knives can be usedin chip carving, including a skewchisel and a gouge, but a regularcarving knife will work just fine.
